paragraphs: Swamiji liked to tell an old joke about a soldier who caught a Tartar. The soldier was out beyond the town, and as he got close to the barracks he shouted that he had captured a Tartar.

Someone inside called back and told him to bring the prisoner in. The soldier replied that the Tartar refused to come. Then come in yourself, said the voice. The soldier's answer: the Tartar would not let him go.

Swamiji said our minds are exactly like this. We think we have got hold of something, but really it has got hold of us. We cannot calm it down, and it will not let us calm down. Everyone talks about being quiet and peaceful, and even a small child imagines it is easy. In truth it is very hard.

He spoke from his own experience. He had dropped all his duties and run off to the mountain tops, lived in caves and in deep forests. Yet even there he found he had 'caught a Tartar', because he carried his whole world with him wherever he went.

The real Tartar, he said, is what lives in our own minds. So we should not blame people or situations outside us, calling some circumstances good and others bad. The trouble is inside. Once we can quieten that inner Tartar, everything will be fine.
learn: Changing your city, college, phone or friend circle will not by itself fix restlessness, because your mind comes along. The useful work is learning to calm and steady your own thoughts, and that skill goes with you everywhere.
